## Description

Phyto-MAP integrates marine phytoplankton abundance records from
published literature, archives, and institutions into a common
relational data model. Abundances are standardised to cells per litre
and linked to available metadata on sources, sampling, dates,
locations, depths, taxonomy, and analytical protocols.

The database retains source-reported taxon designations and associated
curation attributes alongside the taxonomic classifications used
in each release. This structure supports the joint exploration
of heterogeneous observations while preserving the information
needed to interpret their provenance and processing.

## Data and documentation

The distribution includes:

- The relational database in SQLite format.
- Relational CSV exports and a pre-joined export with one row
  per abundance record.
- The database schema and variable dictionary.
- A source bibliography and provenance index.
- Technical-validation documentation and code.
- Citation metadata, a release manifest, and SHA-256 checksums.

## Usage considerations

Differences between sources in sampling effort, analytical methods,
temporal and spatial precision, and taxonomic resolution should
be considered before combining observations.

Retained zeros represent source-specific non-detection of a taxon
under the relevant protocol, not necessarily ecological absence.
Likewise, missing records should not automatically be interpreted
as zero abundance.

Provenance is documented at source and subsource levels;
the database does not provide a universal crosswalk between
every curated record and an identifiable row in the original data.
